text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text:
Add a **large, high-contrast skip link** at the top of every page, visible only when focused.

This lets keyboard users bypass repetitive navigation blocks instantly, solving the biggest keyboard barrier without cluttering the screen for mouse users. The trade-off is a brief visual flash when tabbed to, but that’s minor compared to the accessibility win.

name: Reader
text: The real risk is the skip link becoming a persistent visual element when focused, defeating its purpose. A better alternative is a skip link that appears only after a short delay or on the first tab press, then disappears. Settle it with user testing: measure how often keyboard users miss it versus how often sighted users find it distracting.

name: Ramp
text:
Add a **persistent skip link** at the top of every page, styled with high contrast and visible at all times.

This guarantees keyboard users never miss it, removing the cognitive load of hunting for a hidden control. The trade-off is a small permanent element that may slightly clutter the top of the page for mouse users, but its utility outweighs the minor visual noise.

name: Reader

name: Access
text: DECISION: Implement a **persistent, subtle skip link** (1px by 1px underline) at the top of every page, visible only when keyboard-focused, with high contrast on focus. Ramp owns delivery by EOD Friday.
